document_check.note: The document is Xiao S, Li Y, Liu M, Li Y. 'Electrophysiological evidence of impaired cognitive reappraisal in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: An event-related potential study', Behavioural Brain Research 427 (2022) 113800. It compares late positive potential (LPP) during cognitive reappraisal in 46 aMCI and 47 healthy elderly controls whose HAMD scores did not differ (5.26 vs 5.28, p = 0.97). This matches the cited Xiao et al. 2022a.

cited_result: Principal result: the reappraisal-related LPP difference (Rea - Neg) was smaller in aMCI than in controls in the later time windows (1101-2000 ms t = -2.125, p = .036; 2001-3600 ms p = .064; 3601-5000 ms t = -2.009, p = .048; Condition x Group interaction in 3600-5000 ms p = .020), with no group difference in HAMD depression scores (Table 1). Secondary: a smaller behavioural reduction in arousal ratings in aMCI (t = 3.205, p = 0.002).
tool_reason: The cited result compares an electrophysiological measure between aMCI and control groups at a single time point, and the authors call the design cross-sectional, so the JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist applies.

domains.domain: Item 1. Criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined
domains.rationale: The inclusion and exclusion criteria for both groups are listed in detail.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: Exclusion criteria include: 1) age below 55 years; 2) definite history of stroke; 3) definite history of other diseases of the central nervous system such as infection, demyelinating diseases, and Parkinson's disease; 4) definite history of mental illness such as schizophrenia, major depressive disorder; ... For HECs, the inclusion criteria were as follows: 1) had no complaint of memory/cognitive decline; 2) MMSE > 20 for primary school or above, MMSE > 24 for junior high school or above; 3) the ability to perform daily errands was not impaired; 4) all cognitive domains were within the normal range; and 5) no history of diabetes.

domains.domain: Item 2. Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The recruitment sources for each group and the demographic and clinical profile (Table 1) are reported. The recruitment period is not given. Note the differential post-recruitment exclusion: 26 of 72 aMCI (36%) against 3 of 50 controls, which leaves a better-performing aMCI subset.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: Individuals with aMCI were recruited from the Department of Neurology and the Department of Memory Clinic of Shanghai Tongji Hospital. Age-, gender-, and education-matched HECs were recruited from the community. All participants were Chinese and between 55 and 85 years old.

domains.domain: Item 3. Exposure (group membership) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Group membership was assigned by a neurologist after a full neuropsychological battery given to every participant.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: All participants underwent a comprehensive Neuropsychological Test Battery (NTB) that included the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), the Clinical Dementia Rating scale (CDR) [34], and the Hachinski Ischemic Score (HIS) [35].

domains.domain: Item 4. Objective, standard criteria for the condition
domains.rationale: aMCI was defined by published general criteria with CDR 0.5 and test-based impairment. Depression, needed for the 'equal depression' claim, was measured with the standard HAMD. The exact cut-offs are not stated, and the sample is called multi-domain although the criteria also admit memory-only impairment.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: According to the general criteria for aMCI as defined previously [38], aMCI was designated by a neurologist ... based on the following specific criteria: 1) complaints of memory/cognitive decline by the subject and his caregiver; 2) CDR = .5; 3) any of the following two criteria was met: i) at least two tests within the memory cognitive domain scored below the established cut-off; ii) at least two cognitive domains (memory and other cognitive domains) were impaired.

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education, depression and anxiety were identified and measured in both groups.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: The Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) [36] and the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA) [37] were used to evaluate their symptoms and severity of depression and anxiety.

domains.domain: Item 6. Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated
domains.rationale: Controls were group-matched on age, sex and education, and clinically significant depression and anxiety were excluded by restriction. The resulting HAMD means were almost identical (5.26 vs 5.28, p = 0.97). No covariate adjustment was made in the ERP analyses, and one criterion (no history of diabetes) was applied to controls only.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: Age-, gender-, and education-matched HECs were recruited from the community. ... 9) HIS Score ≥4; 10) HAMD ≥14; 11) HAMA ≥21.

domains.domain: Item 7. Outcomes measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: LPP was recorded with a standard 64-channel system and pipeline. However, the electrode cluster and the four time windows were chosen from the same data, using an exploratory analysis of Group and Condition effects and visual inspection of grand averages, so the outcome was defined after seeing the data. Nothing says whether trial rejection and ICA cleaning were done blind to group.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: we first performed an exploratory analysis of LPP [46–48] to identify the sets of neighbouring electrodes showing LPP modulations by Group and Condition factor. ... we divided the LPP into four time windows ... based on visual inspection of the grand average waveforms and the results of the LPP exploratory analysis.

domains.rationale: The between-group LPP-difference tests were run separately in each of four data-selected windows at alpha 0.05, with no correction across windows. The cited late-window differences rest on p = .036 and p = .048, and the 2001-3600 ms window is non-significant (p = .064). Selecting the electrodes by Group-sensitive exploratory analysis and then testing Group effects at those electrodes is circular and inflates false-positive risk.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: Meanwhile, the LPP amplitude difference (Rea - Neg) of the two groups was tested by independent t-tests in each time window. All analyses were conducted at the 0.05 level of significance. ... Most importantly, MCI showed a smaller LPP difference (Rea - Neg) than HEC in the second (t = −2.125, p = .036), third (t = −1.874, p = .064) and fourth (t = −2.009, p = .048) time windows.

overall: High risk of bias (JBI item 8 'No'; item 7 'Unclear')
overall_rationale: Participant definition, group assignment and depression control are adequate: controls were matched and HAMD-restricted, with near-identical HAMD means. The cited late-window LPP deficit, however, comes from electrodes and windows chosen from the same data (including the Group factor) and from per-window tests without multiplicity control, with p-values just under 0.05. Under this review's rule a 'No' on appropriate analysis makes the overall judgment high. The differential exclusion of 36% of recruited aMCI (unable to complete the task or abnormal behavioural data) adds a further selection concern.

applicability.rationale: A hospital memory-clinic aMCI sample, after excluding 26 of 72 who could not complete the task or had abnormal behavioural data, and after excluding HAMD >= 14. The result may not extend to more impaired or depressed MCI.
